prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1436; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by a third-party vehicle. Police report requested. Insured reports neck stiffness and no airbag deployment. Photos of both vehicles uploaded to file.

Entry 2: Third-party carrier acknowledged liability coverage review. Claimant is now represented by counsel; all further contact to go through the attorney's office. Letter of representation received and logged. Future medical records and wage information to be requested through counsel.

Entry 3: Claimant reports right knee injury from the impact, with pain on bending and swelling noted in a medical summary received from counsel. Treating physician has recommended imaging and physical therapy. Records request sent. Reserve reviewed and increased to reflect possible orthopedic treatment.

Entry 4: Independent medical review scheduled per file procedure. Vehicle repair estimate received and reviewed against photos; damage consistent with reported impact speed. Supervisor notified that claimant's attorney has requested a settlement conference once treatment is complete. No settlement offer to be made until records are in hand.

Entry 5: MRI results received through counsel and reviewed. Findings show a partial meniscus tear in the right knee, consistent with the reported mechanism of injury. Claim file flagged for bodily injury evaluation. Adjuster to coordinate with claims supervisor before any demand response is prepared.
